assumptions: Isentropic, adiabatic, one-dimensional expansion of ideal gases from idea 31's infinite-area-combustor chamber (NASA RP-1311 chapter 6); shifting equilibrium and frozen composition bound the real, finite-rate flow.
Frozen composition from the chamber; species under 1e-10 mole fraction left out of the frozen mixture.
Divergence efficiency applied to the vacuum thrust coefficient, as SP-125 Figure 4-12 defines it; no boundary-layer, kinetic or combustion-efficiency losses.
Separation by SP-8120's criterion with the one-dimensional exit pressure standing for the exit wall pressure; a separated nozzle's thrust is bracketed, not predicted.
C_F at ambient pa: C_F(pa) = C_F,vac - eps pa / pc while the nozzle flows full (pa below separation_onset_ambient_pressure).
Frames and time scales: none (a nozzle has no position or epoch).

assumptions: Thrust chamber: idea 31's equilibrium chamber and idea 32's shifting nozzle, re-run at every throttle point at the same mixture ratio and geometry; delivered c* = eta_c* x ideal c*, vacuum C_F = eta_CF x divergence efficiency x ideal, both efficiencies held over the throttle range.
F(pa) = F_vac - pa x exit_area while the nozzle flows full (pa below separation_onset_ambient_pressure); mass flow does not depend on altitude.
Ambient pressure from the 1976 US Standard Atmosphere (PartForge isa(), via ideas 02 and 32), 0 to 86 km; vacuum above.

Pumps incompressible (power = mdot dp / (rho eta)); turbines isentropic drop x efficiency; every cycle parameter (pressure ladder, efficiencies, inlet temperatures, routing) from the named reference engine, held over the throttle range.
Frames and time scales: none (an engine deck has no position or epoch).
